cost: BOTH SUBJECTS LAND INSIDE THEIR BANDS AND NEITHER LANDS ON ITS CENTRE, and the reason is not the ramp. Malik Beasley '23 reads 56 against 58 +-3 and Buddy Hield '25 reads 58 against 58 +-3. Beasley '23's remaining gap to his own '22 is NOT a cliff any more: it is three points of the weapon (89 against 92, worth 0.075 of zone_f) plus seven points of usage and a ball-security fall of ten. Hield's is recal_96's load share — 22.7 minutes against 25.7. Both are measured differences that the formula is supposed to price, which is why the round stops at the gate.

THE WIDTH IS NOT SET BY THE ANCHORS, AND THAT IS SAID PLAINLY. Every width from 2 to 10 holds all 137 pins AND puts both subjects inside their bands (Beasley reads 55, 56, 56, 57, 57, 57, 57 and Hield 57, 58, 59, 59, 59, 59, 60 at widths 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10). What sets it is the collateral, which runs 42 movers at 2, 70 at 3, 97 at 4, 131 at 5, 156 at 6, 213 at 8, 264 at 10 — so the round takes the NARROWEST width that reaches both numbers, and the derivation (the class's own lower-quartile deficit of 3.25) sits inside that choice rather than being reverse-engineered from it.

COLLATERAL IS 70 CARDS ON OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM UP, mean +1.93, max +5. NOTHING ON THE BOARD MOVES BY 8 OR MORE ON ANY SCALE. Three cards move by 5 (the two subjects and Lonzo Ball '21), three by 4, eleven by 3. OVR follows on 58, max +3. DEF moves on ZERO cards and every attribute on ZERO. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant and no leaver — the only card in it that moves at all is Tim Duncan '04, 91 -> 92.

THE ONE STAR THE ROUND TOUCHES IS TIM DUNCAN '04, and he is the defect rather than the collateral. rim 90 against the gate's flat bar of 91: one point short of the paint bonus recal_46 built for exactly his damage, and he printed 85. He now reads 88 and OVR 92. Chris Webber '95 (rim 89) is the same card one notch down, 72 -> 75. They are the only two paint cards in the top 25 movers, because recal_51's own volume ramp zeroes the attempt factor for every low-usage interior man newly inside the ramp.

WHAT IS STILL A CLIFF, and a later ruling would have to name it. TWO tests inside this gate are deliberately left hard. `max(3pt, rim) >= mid` is recal_38's ruling that a towering MIDRANGE is not the same threat — a statement about WHICH zone, which has no 'how much' to ramp. `z[0] > z[1] + z[2]` inside clause 1 is the towering claim itself: a card at z[0] = 91 whose second and third zones sum to 91 gets nothing from clause 1 and must go through clause 2. Both are shape identity rather than degree, which is why r43's 'no cliffs' does not reach them.

BYTE-IDENTITY IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED. Every card at or above either bar has its o_score raw compared to ten decimal places before and after: Korver '15 61.9200000000, Kerr '96 65.6246231250, Reggie Miller '97 93.7618000000, Curry '16 104.9130000000, Novak '13 67.1228571429, Shaq '00 113.7656370155, Capela '17 61.6535166667, Zion '21 96.8846305220, Giannis '25 118.5676998812, Tolliver '14, Bowen '06, Snell '18 — all identical. The five tol-1 shooter pins the dispatch named are the first five of that list.

THE BAND ANCHORS ARE NOT TOUCHED. Every one of the 70 movers is below the 93 knee, where band() is the identity, so OFF_TOP (102.75) and DEF_TOP (104.25) are byte-identical and no card above the knee moves at all — including Giannis '25, the card recal_90 derived OFF_TOP from.

notes: THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: recal_43 ruled 'NO CLIFFS' and turned every factor INSIDE the zone-dominance bonus into a line, but whether a bonus worth 5 to 8 raw points was paid AT ALL was still decided by two hard tests — so one point of one zone rating decided seven printed OFF points.

BOTH SUBJECTS ARE EXACTLY ONE POINT SHORT, which is the defect in its purest form. Malik Beasley '23's zones are 89 / 44 / 16, and clause 2's bar for him is 1.5 x (44 + 16) = 90. Buddy Hield '25's are 90 / 38 / 27, and clause 1's bar is the flat 91. Neither man is a different player from the season beside him; each is one rating point on the wrong side of a `>`.

IT IS NOT TWO CARDS. Of the 217 adjacent-season pairs of the same SHOOTER where this gate fires on one season and not the other, 65 flip on a three-point move of 4 or less; the paint class has 295 such pairs of its own, 238 of them on a 3pt move of 4 or less.

THE TWO CLAUSES ALWAYS SAID THE SAME THING, and that is what makes ONE constant enough. Both are 'the weapon must reach a bar'; they differ only in where the bar is — the flat 91 for the man whose zone is elite outright, and 1.5 x (z[1] + z[2]) for recal_37's 'true narrow specialist whose zone is not yet 91'. Writing both ramps in the SAME unit (points of z[0] beneath the card's own bar) means the round adds one number rather than four, and the two clauses cannot drift apart.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool at seven widths — 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 — Beasley reads 55, 56, 56, 57, 57, 57, 57 and Hield 57, 58, 59, 59, 59, 59, 60, with 42, 70, 97, 131, 156, 213, 264 movers. All 137 anchors hold at every one of them and every mover is UP at every one of them.

TWO EARLIER SHAPES WERE BUILT AND MEASURED FIRST, and both are worse. Ramping ONLY the ratio clause, from the dominance line 1.0 up to its own 1.5, reaches both numbers (Beasley 58, Hield 59) but moves 419 cards — six times the collateral for the same two rulings, because it pays a partial bonus to every card whose best zone merely leads. Ramping the two clauses on their OWN units instead (z[0] over 87 -> 91 and the ratio over 1.4 -> 1.5) reaches 57 and 59 at 106 movers, but it needs TWO constants in two different units and neither of them is measured on anything.

DEF MOVES ON ZERO CARDS BY CONSTRUCTION. The bonus is a term inside o_score; d_score does not read it, is_big does not read it, and build_ratings.py was not run, so no attribute on any of the 10,000 cards changed.
